title: Constructing Water Retention Structures
status: draft: written 18 Nov 2026 offline for Grade 7 Agriculture; not yet checked by a CBC Agriculture teacher; not loaded by the live tutor
notes: Dig a retention ditch across the slope or a retention pit (about 60 cm wide and deep) with a raised bank on the downhill side, then plant a banana sucker, napier grass or arrowroot in or beside it. Digging only with the teacher present.

skills.key_step: The child describes how surface run-off can be used in gardening (led into retention ditches, pits and water pans to water crops, slowed by mulch and grass) instead of being lost and causing erosion.

floor.question: How should a slope be ploughed?

representations: a tilted tray with and without a ditch
pictures of a water pan and a retention pit
a compound sketch with water paths
steps: Lead it into a ditch, pit or pan.
Slow the rest with mulch and grass.

board.do: Draw a slope with arrows of run-off to a road.
Ask how the water could help a garden instead.
Draw a retention pit catching the water beside a banana.

misconceptions.ask: What can be done with surface run-off?
misconceptions.repair: Follow run-off after rain to a low place where plants grow green; ask what it could water.
Compare water poured on a bare tray and on a tray with a small ditch dug across it.

misconceptions.ask: What does mulch do to run-off?
misconceptions.repair: Pour water on a tilted bare tray and a mulched tray; time how fast it runs off each.

listen_for: Only rain falling straight into the pit
misconceptions.ask: Which water can be led into a retention pit?
misconceptions.repair: Trace where the roof water goes after a storm.

checks.question: What is surface run-off?
checks.answer: rain water flowing over the ground

checks.question: Name a structure that holds run-off.
checks.answer: a retention ditch, retention pit or water pan

skills.key_step: The child says how a retention ditch or pit is built: find where run-off flows, mark across the slope, dig (about 60 cm wide and deep), soil on the downhill side as a bank, add manure, plant a water-loving crop, clear silt after rain.

floor.prerequisite: Knows how run-off can be used.
floor.question: Where can run-off be led?

steps: Dig; bank on the downhill side.

board.do: Draw a slope with a ditch across it.
Ask which side the soil bank goes.

misconceptions.ask: How is a retention ditch laid out on a slope?
misconceptions.repair: Pour water down a tray with a ditch down the slope and one across it.

misconceptions.ask: Where is the dug soil put when making a retention ditch?
misconceptions.repair: Model both on a tray; see which holds the water in the ditch.

misconceptions.ask: Which crop suits a retention pit that stays wet?
misconceptions.repair: Ask which crops grow in wet valley bottoms.

misconceptions.ask: Why must a retention ditch be cleared after heavy rain?
misconceptions.repair: Show a ditch half filled with silt after a season.

checks.question: Why is a retention ditch dug across the slope?
checks.answer: to catch run-off instead of speeding it up

checks.question: Name a crop to plant in a retention pit.
checks.answer: bananas, arrowroot, sugarcane or napier grass
